title: Replacing Dicky Wells in Bill Coleman's band
summary: Coleman's group worked clubs in Switzerland and Germany, but Dicky Wells and Zutty Singleton had tired of it. Waters accepted Coleman's offer, hoping the band would reach Paris.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Uh huh. How did that come about?

Well, Dicky Wells was working with Bill Coleman at the point. And Bill was doing the, working [ ] clubs, you know - club dates, see, weekend, weekday, like that, see. And some of them Germany also. And Bill was from Paris, too, he live in Paris.

Yeah. So then Dicky Wells just got tired. We didn't even have Zutty Singleton on the job, we had Zutty there with him. And Zutty got tired, you can read that thing in "Down Beat" about that, too, Zutty did. He got tired, he said all musicians in Europe were starving, which is not true, see. That's what he said, see. But it was a lot of musicians out of work (laughs), that, you know, is true. Negro musicians, I mean, is true. So I had a chance to join him on account of Dicky Wells just got tired and left. It was work, he was working with Bill, but he got tired, as Bill says. Then Bill and, Bill asked me, would I want to join the band. So - just like I'm talkin' about New York - the first thing, when he asked me that, I'm not thinkin' about no Switzerland, I'm thinkin' about Paris. See what I mean? So I said "Yes, I want to go to Paris". I didn't say exactly that, but that's what my mind was thinkin'. I said "This would be a lot [ ]" -
'Cause you knew Coleman would end up in Paris sooner or later -
Sure would, that's his home, he was on a tour -

you see? So I said "That's my", he didn't say nothin' but I'm ambitious, I meant "Now I'll get to Paris". So - which I did. See, so finally I go, we stayed around this for a little bit longer, see. And we, I played with Zutty a few nights only, I think. And Zutty left, too. And we got another job -
